summary.whatChanges: Collapses Zod's two lazy-value helpers into one: `util.cached` now returns the prototype-backed `Cached` box (previously `cachedInternal`), and `cachedInternal` is removed. Object, JIT object, and discriminated-union schemas now call `cached`. Tests are rewritten to cover the single implementation.
behaviorChanges: `util.cachedInternal` no longer exists as an export.
Boxes from `util.cached` no longer have an own enumerable `value`: `Object.keys(box)` is empty and spreading yields `{}`.
`value` is now inherited from a shared prototype instead of being redefined as an own property on first read.
`util.allowsEval` and internal schema caches (object shape normalization, discriminated-union map) use the new box shape.
Cached boxes carry two state slots instead of a self-replacing accessor, per the stated memory/access-cost rationale.
risks: `z.core.util.cached` is public; consumers relying on the own enumerable `value` (spread, `Object.keys`, JSON serialization, structuredClone) will silently get an empty object.
Any code still importing `util.cachedInternal` breaks at build or runtime.
Boxes now retain the getter reference in `_getter` and expose `_value`/`_getter` slots that were not previously observable.
Dropped test coverage for property-descriptor semantics means regressions in box shape would go unnoticed.
